# Donate to Jamie Yee for City Council!
Pitch in today to support Jamie Yee for Pleasanton City Council - District 3. Together, we will be learn from the past while we plan responsibly for our future—protecting property values, keeping residents safe, supporting a strong local economy, and preserving the community character that makes Pleasanton a place we are proud to call home.
________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Contributions to this committee are not tax-deductible.
An individual at least 18 years of age, organization, business, or corporation may contribute to this committee under California law. Donor reporting is required by the City of Pleasanton for contributions totaling $25 or more. Cash contributions of $100 or more, cashier’s checks or money orders of $100 or more, and contributions from foreign nationals are prohibited. The maximum contribution limit is $5,900 per person per election. Titles are for identification purposes only.

# Welcome and Thank You for Visiting!
Pleasanton is special because of the choices we make—protecting our neighborhoods, planning carefully, and investing in what matters most.
Jamie Yee brings a deep, personal connection to Pleasanton. Her parents moved her family here in 1969 from Berkeley, when open fields, farms, ranches and no traffic signals were part of everyday life. That history shapes Jamie’s belief that the decisions we make today must be thoughtful, transparent, and grounded in long-term planning.
Jamie has dedicated more than two decades to public service in this community, including 12 years as an elected Trustee on the Pleasanton Unified School District Board, over 10 years as a PTA Leader, eight years on the City of Pleasanton Economic Vitality Committee, and four years on the City of Pleasanton Civic Arts Commission. Her two now-adult children were raised here in Pleasanton, attending K-12 in PUSD. This has always been — and will always be — home.
Jamie is committed to leadership that learns from our past while planning responsibly for our future—protecting property values, keeping residents safe, supporting a strong local economy, and preserving the community character that makes Pleasanton a place people are proud to call home. Jamie is an experienced candidate who will represent District 3 with unwavering commitment once elected on November 3, 2026.
